conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice. Spatial integration uses Q_d = R^d/(2πZ)^d with probability volume (2π)^(-d) dx; the L2 norm uses that normalization.
The Leray multiplier retains the zero mode: P_0 = I; for nonzero k, P_k = I − kkᵀ/|k|². Tensor divergence is (div F)_i = Σ_j ∂_j F_ij.

The residual is r_v = ∂_t v + P div(v⊗v) − νΔv − Pf, with ν ≥ 0. Fields are smooth; the certificate assumes an already supplied smooth exact solution and controls a continuous-domain residual, not finitely many collocation values.
The spatial Jacobian has entries (∇_x u)_ij = ∂_j u_i. A(t) integrates the spatial supremum of its Euclidean operator norm. Only u_0, u, and v must be divergence-free; f is arbitrary.
The training law is μ and the target law is ν(E) = ∫_E g dμ, where g ≥ 0, ∫g dμ = 1, and g ≤ C almost everywhere for finite C ≥ 1. The error hypothesis is a population mean-square bound.

The counterexample uses the power-set measurable space {0,1}, training law δ_0, target law δ_1, and arbitrary M > 0. Its conclusion excludes a uniform target-bias bound based solely on training-law error.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated smooth periodic data and solenoidal comparison field, define r_v := ∂_t v + P div(v⊗v) − νΔv − Pf and d_0 := ‖v(0) − u_0‖_2. The residual belongs to C([0,T];L2), and its time-integrated L2 norm is finite.

For measurable maps S and S̃ into a real normed space with finite second moments under probability μ, an L-Lipschitz real observable J, population error ∫‖S−S̃‖² dμ ≤ ε², and target density 0 ≤ g ≤ C with ∫g dμ = 1, both target observables are integrable and |E_ν[J(S)] − E_ν[J(S̃)]| ≤ L√C ε.

Under Countable Choice, on the normalized periodic torus in dimension 2 or 3, let ν ≥ 0 and let u and v be smooth divergence-free fields with common smooth forcing, u(0)=u_0, and ∂_t u + P div(u⊗u) − νΔu = Pf. With the stated residual and A(t)=∫_0^t sup_x ‖∇_x u(s,x)‖_op ds, every t ∈ [0,T] satisfies ‖v(t)−u(t)‖_2 ≤ exp(A(t))(‖v(0)−u_0‖_2 + ∫_0^t exp(−A(s))‖r_v(s)‖_2 ds).

The law-shift proposition supplies its own norm-Borel state space, measurable maps, Lipschitz observable, and moments; it imports no sampling, selection, or physical-validity guarantee.

This is a page prerequisite rather than an invocation of the periodic theorem: the common-wall theorem supplies an independent bounded-domain proof.
